title.rendered: Easiest IGCSE Subjects: Pass Rates, Picks & Cautions 2026

content.rendered:
Key Summary

  • Easiest By The Data: ESL, Business Studies, Drama, Music, and Environmental Management consistently post the highest pass rates in Cambridge’s June 2024 IGCSE results.
  • “Easy” Has Two Meanings: The subjects easiest to pass at grade C/4 are not always the easiest to score A* in, and mixing these up leads to poor choices.
  • UAE Schools Split Boards: Most Dubai schools follow either Cambridge (CIE) or Pearson Edexcel, and your “easy” pick depends partly on which board your school uses.
  • Watch The University Trade-Off: Picking only soft subjects can close doors for A-Levels, UCAS, and competitive degree pathways like medicine or engineering.
  • Profile Beats Pass Rate: A high pass-rate subject in a topic you find boring is harder than a moderate-rate subject you actually enjoy.

If you’re in Year 9 at a Dubai international school, you’ve probably been handed a subject options form and told to “choose wisely.” That’s not particularly helpful advice when you’re deciding between eight or nine IGCSEs, and every option feels like a guess.

What most students really want to know is simple: which subjects give me the best shot at strong grades without making my life miserable for two years? This guide answers that using Cambridge’s own June 2024 results data, not opinions. We’ll also cover what UAE students specifically should consider

If you’re sitting Cambridge O-Levels rather than IGCSEs, most of the subjects and pass rate data here applies equally, since Cambridge publishes combined statistics for both qualifications. At Ignite Training Institute, we work with IGCSE students across Dubai every week, and subject selection is one of the first conversations we have with new families.

What Counts As An “Easy” IGCSE Subject?

The easiest IGCSE subjects are those with high pass rates, lower content volume, practical or coursework-based assessments, and topics that connect to everyday knowledge rather than abstract theory. But “easy” genuinely depends on the student. A subject with a 90% pass rate globally can still feel challenging if it doesn’t match your strengths.

There are three ways to measure difficulty, and they tell different stories.

Pass Rate (Grade C / 4 And Above)

This is the most common metric. Cambridge International publishes cumulative results after every June and November series. A pass rate of 90%+ at grade C suggests most students manage the subject comfortably. But this number can be misleading because it includes native speakers sitting language exams (who naturally push the pass rate higher) and doesn’t tell you how hard it is to do well, only how hard it is not to fail.

A*/A Achievement Rate

This is what competitive students actually care about. Some subjects have a high pass rate but a very low A* rate, meaning the baseline is accessible, but reaching the top requires real effort. Drama is a good example: 89% of students pass at C+, but only 8.4% reach A*. If you’re aiming for top grades, the A* rate matters more than the pass rate.

Workload And Assessment Format

Subjects with heavy coursework (like Art and Design or Drama) might have generous pass rates, but they ask for consistent effort across the entire course, not just exam-week revision. Others, like Business Studies, are assessed entirely by written exams, which suits students who work well under time pressure and prefer shorter revision windows.

How Your Profile Changes The Answer

A student who reads constantly will find English Literature approachable. A student who thinks in numbers might breeze through Accounting but find History tough going. The data gives us a starting point, but your own learning style is the filter you apply on top of it.

Know More About: IGCSE Grades Explained: Grading System, Pass Marks 2026

Easiest IGCSE Subjects Based On Cambridge June 2024 Pass Rates

Here’s what Cambridge’s official June 2024 statistics actually show for the subjects commonly considered “easy.” We’ve included both the C+ pass rate and the A* rate so you can see the full picture.

A few things stand out from this table.

English As A Second Language (0510)

ESL is probably the most commonly recommended “easy” IGCSE, and for many UAE students, it is genuinely manageable. The exam tests practical communication: reading short texts, writing emails or reports, listening comprehension, and a speaking test. There’s no literary analysis, no creative writing under pressure, no essay structure to master.

That said, notice the A* rate: only 10.6%. Getting a comfortable pass is one thing. Scoring an A* requires precise reading comprehension, accurate grammar, and strong listening skills at speed. If you’re already confident in English and your school offers it, ESL is a solid pick. But if you’re a native English speaker, your school may not offer it, and you’d sit First Language English instead, which is a different exam entirely.

Business Studies (0450)

Business is popular because the content maps onto things students already understand. Marketing, finance, operations, human resources: these topics connect to real companies and real decisions. The exam format is structured questions and case studies, so you’re applying logic and common sense rather than recalling pure theory.

Worth knowing: only 9.9% reach A*. To do well, you need clear, structured writing and the ability to apply frameworks to unfamiliar case studies, not just memorise definitions. Students who put in consistent effort throughout the two years tend to do well. The ones who expect a free pass sometimes find the grade doesn’t reflect what they hoped.

ICT (0417)

ICT covers practical computing skills: spreadsheets, databases, web design, and presentation software, plus theoretical knowledge about how data is stored, transmitted, and used. Students who already use computers daily often find the practical component straightforward.

The practical exam (where you actually use software to solve tasks) tends to be where students pick up strong marks, because it rewards doing rather than memorising. The theory paper is lighter than Computer Science (0478) but still requires focused revision.

Environmental Management (0680)

This subject sits at the intersection of geography and biology. It covers ecosystems, climate, resource use, pollution, and conservation. Students who like reading about real-world problems but prefer a lighter mathematical load than Physics or a lower memorisation demand than Biology often gravitate here.

Assessment is two exam papers, no coursework. The content is current, relatable, and less abstract than traditional sciences. It’s also less widely offered in Dubai schools than in Southeast Asia or Africa, so check your school’s options list before assuming it’s available.

Drama (0411) And Music (0410)

Both have strong pass rates (89% and 92% respectively). Drama is 60% practical assessment (solo and group performances), which suits students who are comfortable performing. Music requires you to perform, compose, and complete a listening exam. If you have musical training, the practical elements are where you earn your marks.

Both subjects work well for students with a genuine interest and some existing skills. They’re not easy in the “minimal effort” sense. They’re accessible because the work feels engaging rather than heavy when you enjoy the subject. That’s an important difference.

Know More About: How To Get Good Grades In Biology: 10 Proven Tips

Easiest IGCSE Subjects For UAE Students Specifically

Most guides on this topic are written for a UK or global audience. If you’re studying in Dubai or the wider UAE, a few things are different.

Native-Language Subjects: Arabic And First Language Picks

Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544) has a 92.0% C+ pass rate. But for students who speak Arabic at home, the real opportunity is Arabic as a First Language (0508): 66.8% at C+ with 14.4% reaching A*. That’s a strong performance profile for a subject you already use every day. If your school offers it, this is one of the most natural paths to a high grade.

The same logic applies to other first-language options. First Language Urdu, First Language Hindi, First Language Turkish: if you’re already fluent, these become comfortable picks that can strengthen your overall transcript.

ESL Vs First Language English For South Asian Dubai Students

This is one of the most common subject-selection dilemmas for families in Dubai. Many South Asian students speak English fluently at home and at school, but their passport language is different. Schools sometimes allow these students to take ESL (0510) instead of First Language English (0500).

The trade-off: ESL is more accessible to pass (67.3% vs 83.6% at C+), but First Language English is what most UK universities expect for competitive courses. If you’re planning to apply to Russell Group universities through UCAS, check their IGCSE requirements before defaulting to ESL. Some universities accept ESL. Others don’t. It’s worth a quick check early rather than a surprise later.

Cambridge Vs Pearson Edexcel: Does The Board Matter?

About half of Dubai’s KHDA-licensed international schools run Cambridge (CIE) IGCSEs. The rest use Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and a small number offer Oxford AQA. The syllabus content is similar, but the exam format differs: Cambridge tends toward structured, tiered papers (Core and Extended), while Edexcel uses a single-tier approach.

For most students, the board doesn’t dramatically change which subjects feel easier. But it does affect how exams feel. Some students prefer Cambridge’s tiered approach because the Core paper provides a safety net. Others prefer Edexcel’s single paper because there’s no ceiling on the marks they can achieve. Ask your school which boards they use for each subject, as some schools mix boards across departments.

Islamiyat (0493) For Students In MOE-Aligned Schools

Islamiyat is a compulsory or popular optional subject in many UAE schools, particularly those aligned with Ministry of Education requirements. The June 2024 Cambridge data shows a 79.6% pass rate at C+, with 15.6% reaching A*. For students with a religious studies background, this can be a comfortable addition to the IGCSE subject list.

Know More About: Edexcel vs Cambridge: Key Differences You Should Know 2026

Subjects That Seem Easy But Need More Effort Than Expected

Some subjects have strong pass rates or accessible-sounding content, but students regularly underestimate the work involved. This isn’t to discourage you from picking them. It’s just worth going in with realistic expectations so you can prepare properly.

Drama: High Pass Rate, Consistent Coursework Commitment

Drama’s 89% pass rate is encouraging. But 60% of the grade comes from practical performances that need rehearsal, group coordination, and in some cases, devised pieces that students create from scratch. Students who stay on top of rehearsals and engage with the group element tend to do well. The written exam (40%) also involves analysis of theatrical techniques, which requires its own study time alongside the practical work.

First Language English: Fluency Alone Isn’t Enough

First Language English (0500) has an 83.6% pass rate at C+, which seems comfortable. But the A* rate is only 12.9%. The exam asks for directed writing, creative composition, and analysis of unseen passages under time pressure. 

Being a native speaker helps with comprehension, but exam technique is what separates a B from an A*. Students who read widely and practise timed writing tend to see better results than those who rely on fluency alone.

Sociology: Approachable Content, Demanding Exams

Sociology’s content is interesting and relatable: social structures, inequality, education, and family. The challenge is that the exam requires essay-length responses with sociological terminology, theoretical frameworks, and critical evaluation. Only 5.4% of students scored A* in June 2024, and 26.6% reached A or above. It’s a subject where genuine interest in the content helps enormously, and pairing that interest with structured essay practice makes a real difference.

Art And Design: Creative Freedom Requires Discipline

Art has a 62.4% pass rate at C+. The portfolio-based assessment gives students creative freedom, but it also requires sustained, self-directed work across the entire course. Students who are naturally artistic and enjoy long-term creative projects tend to thrive. The key is understanding early on that Art requires regular studio time, not just a burst of effort before the deadline.

Know More About: Triple Science VS Combined Science: What To Choose?

How To Choose The Easiest IGCSE Subjects Without Hurting Your Future?

Picking accessible subjects feels smart in Year 9. The key is making sure those choices still keep your future options open when it’s time for A-Levels or IB.

Map Subjects To Your A-Level And IB Plans

If you think you might want to study Biology, Chemistry, or Physics at A-Level, you typically need the corresponding IGCSE at grade B or above. Dropping all three sciences at IGCSE in favour of lighter options closes the door on A-Level sciences at most Dubai schools.

The same applies to Maths: if you don’t take Extended Maths at IGCSE, many schools won’t allow A-Level Mathematics. Planning backward from A-Level (or IB) is the safest approach.

Medicine, Engineering, Law: Balance Easy Picks With Essential Subjects

Medicine requires Biology and Chemistry at IGCSE (and ideally A-Level). Engineering requires Maths and Physics. Law at UK universities values strong grades in essay-based subjects like History or English Literature.

You can absolutely take two or three more accessible subjects alongside these core requirements. Think of it as balancing the workload: keep the essential subjects for your pathway, and use your remaining slots for picks that play to your strengths. That way you get both strong grades and a clear route forward.

UAE University Minimum IGCSE Requirements

UAE-based universities typically require five or more IGCSEs at grade C/4 or above, including English and Mathematics. Universities like Heriot-Watt Dubai,Middlesex University Dubai, and the University of Birmingham Dubai publish specific subject requirements for their degree programmes. If you’re considering staying in the UAE for university, check these entry requirements before finalising your IGCSE subjects. Five passes in subjects that don’t match your degree’s prerequisites may not meet the criteria.

A 4-Step Subject Selection Checklist

Here’s a practical framework:

Step 1:  Lock in the compulsory subjects first. Most schools require a minimum of 5 to 7 IGCSEs, and English, Maths, and at least one science are near-universal requirements. Some Dubai schools also mandate a language and a humanities subject. Start here before thinking about “easy” picks, because these are non-negotiable.

Step 2: Identify the subjects your future career path needs. If you don’t know your career path yet, keep one science, one humanities subject, and one language open. That keeps your options flexible.

Step 3: Fill remaining slots with subjects that play to your strengths. This is where the “easiest IGCSE subjects” list becomes useful, as long as these picks complement your core subjects rather than replace anything important.

Step 4: Cross-check against your school’s board (Cambridge or Edexcel), available teachers, and class timetable. A subject on paper is only as good as the teaching and resources behind it at your school.

Know More About: IGCSE Subjects For Medicine: Ideal Options For Students

Ignite: IGCSE Tutors In Dubai Helping You Pick And Master The Right Subjects

Subject selection is the first step. What comes after is two years of revision, past papers, and exam technique building. That’s where structured tutoring makes the difference.

At Ignite, our IGCSE tutors in Dubai work with students across Cambridge and Edexcel boards, covering every subject from Business Studies and ESL to Physics and Additional Mathematics. We start with a diagnostic to understand where a student stands, then build a revision plan around their exam board’s syllabus, real past paper patterns, and the specific areas where they need the most support.

One parent recently shared that their daughter achieved A* grades across Math, Physics, Chemistry, and Biology after working with Ignite’s tutors. The family credited the personalised attention and the tutor’s willingness to address specific weak areas rather than following a generic lesson plan. That kind of result comes from knowing the syllabus inside out and tailoring the approach to the individual student.

Whether you’ve picked what you think are the easiest IGCSE subjects or you’re taking on some of the more demanding ones, the right support makes any subject more manageable. Book a free demo class and see how a structured study plan changes the way revision feels.

FAQs

1. What Is The Single Easiest IGCSE Subject To Pass?

Based on Cambridge June 2024 data, English as an Additional Language has the highest pass rate at 96.4%, followed by Music (92.0%) and First Language Chinese (95.5%). But these are often taken by students already proficient in the language. For a broader answer: Business Studies, ESL, and Environmental Management are consistently approachable for a wide range of students.

2. Are Combined Sciences Easier Than Triple Science?

Yes, for most students. Combined Science (0653) covers Biology, Chemistry, and Physics in one qualification with less depth per subject. Co-ordinated Sciences (0654) is a step up, offering two separate grades. Triple Science means sitting three full IGCSEs (Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625), each with its own extended syllabus. If you don’t plan to study sciences at A-Level, Combined Science is the lighter option.

3. Is Edexcel IGCSE Easier Than Cambridge?

Neither board is objectively easier. Cambridge uses tiered papers (Core and Extended), which means lower-ability students can sit a simpler paper but are capped at grade C. Edexcel uses a single tier, meaning everyone sits the same exam, and the full grade range is available. Some students prefer one format over the other. The content overlap is roughly 80-85%.

4. What Is The Easiest IGCSE Subject For Non-Native English Speakers?

ESL (0510) is specifically designed for non-native speakers and focuses on practical communication rather than literary analysis. For students whose English is intermediate, ESL provides a structured path to a solid grade. If English is still developing, pairing ESL with a first-language option (Arabic, Urdu, Hindi, Turkish) adds another strong subject to the transcript.

5. Which IGCSE Subjects Have The Highest A* Rates?

From the June 2024 data: Mandarin Chinese as a Foreign Language (74.5%), Malay (70.8%), Italian (64.2%), Arabic (57.0%), and English as an Additional Language (56.5%). These are largely native or near-native speaker cohorts, which lifts the A* rate. Among more widely taken subjects, Additional Mathematics (27.0%), Physics (22.1%), and Chemistry (18.0%) have solid A* rates but are more demanding overall.

6. What Are The Hardest IGCSE Subjects To Avoid?

Based on the data, subjects with the lowest pass rates (C+) include Additional Mathematics (87.3%, but with a challenging extended syllabus), History (73.0%), and Sanskrit (55.6%). That said, “hardest” is personal. A student passionate about history who writes strong essays may find it more enjoyable and manageable than a student picking Environmental Management just because someone told them it was easy.

Know More About: Is O Level And IGCSE The Same? Differences & How To Choose

Conclusion

Choosing your IGCSE subjects doesn’t have to be a gamble. Use Cambridge’s own data to understand which subjects have the highest pass rates, but also look at the A* rates and the assessment format. Factor in your own strengths and what you actually enjoy studying, because two years is a long time to spend on a subject you picked only because someone told you it was easy.

If you’re based in Dubai, think about the board your school uses, whether ESL or First Language English is the right fit, and how your IGCSE choices feed into A-Level or IB pathways. And if you want a second opinion on your options or support once you’ve made your choice, get in touch with Ignite’s academic team or try a free demo class.
